title: Coral and the Colony
premise: Felix Winterbourne, a memory-smuggler hauling contraband recollections through contested orbits, intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries and traces it to a derelict colony ship where two cryogenic populations — the original colonists and the engineered crew who mutinied to save the reactor — wait in suspended animation. The ship's dying AI can wake only half before the reactor fails, and both factions' memories, which Felix has been secretly trafficking for years, hold the truth of who betrayed whom. Forced to choose between the found family she's built among the smuggler crews and the descendants of the people whose stolen memories she sold, Felix wakes the engineered crew, sacrificing her own cached memories of twelve years of friendship to buy the reactor time. The novel ends with the colony ship limping toward a habitable moon, Felix unable to remember why the strangers around her keep calling her family — until one of them plays back a memory she thought she'd erased.
about_author: Ada Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for cryogenic storage systems before turning to fiction. She writes near-future science fiction about people who trade in intangibles — memories, loyalties, time.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Quiet
chapters.summary: Felix smuggles a cache of black-market memories past orbital customs aboard her freighter, establishing her world, her crew of misfits, and the rules of her trade. When an impossible distress signal arrives in a dead language, she recognizes it from a memory chip she sold years ago. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: restless competence shadowed by loneliness — she has everyone's memories but keeps none of her own.

chapters.title: The Ship That Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix boards the derelict colony ship Halcyon and discovers two cryobays: original colonists and the engineered crew who seized the ship mid-voyage. The failing AI forces a choice — only half can wake before reactor failure. The AI reveals Felix's own smuggled memories contain the mutiny's true record. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dawning horror as she realizes she has profited from both sides' grief.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: As the reactor countdown accelerates, Felix races through the ship's memory archives, uncovering that the engineered crew saved the colonists once already — and were condemned for it. Her smuggler allies arrive demanding their cut, forcing her to choose between them and the sleepers. POV: Felix, with interludes from the AI's fragmented logs. Emotional beat: the climax — she wakes the engineered crew and feeds her own twelve years of memories into the reactor buffer.

chapters.title: What the Strangers Call Me
chapters.summary: The Halcyon limps toward a habitable moon with Felix unable to remember her crew, her trade, or why she came. The awakened engineers care for a woman they've never met but whose memories bought their lives. In the final scene, one of them returns a copy of her erased past, and she chooses whether to remember. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — found family rebuilt from loss, memory reclaimed by choice rather than commerce.
